narrative_purpose: Shows how a thick atmosphere flattens the equator-to-pole temperature gap: a thin-aired world has a scorched bright middle and frozen dark poles, while a thick-aired world wrapped in a deep glowing atmosphere runs nearly one even temperature everywhere.
subject: Two planetary spheres side by side. The left sphere is bare and thin-aired: a fiercely bright hot band across its middle fading to dark, deep-frozen poles, a stark contrast from centre to top and bottom. The right sphere is wrapped in a thick, deep, softly glowing atmospheric shell, and its colour is almost uniform from equator to pole - the middle only a little brighter than the edges, the whole globe held at one gentle even tone.
scene: Both spheres in the same dark space; the right one visibly haloed by a thick luminous layer of atmosphere, the left one sharp-edged and airless-looking.
camera: Front-on view of both spheres at equal scale, side by side.
light: Left sphere: harsh hot highlight at the equator, deep cold shadow at the poles. Right sphere: soft, even, diffused glow across the whole disc.
palette: Left: hot amber equator to void-indigo frozen poles, high contrast. Right: even cool teal-cyan everywhere, low contrast, thick misty-cyan atmospheric halo.
style: Painterly plate reading as a comparison diagram, soft glowing atmosphere on the right, NOT a vector chart, NOT a 3D render.
detail_level: Moderate: the key is the contrast - stark gradient on the left, near-uniform tone on the right.
composition: Two equal spheres balanced left and right, the left high-contrast and bare, the right low-contrast and thickly haloed, dark space between.
consistency_notes: Warm amber reserved for the thin world's overheated equator; the thick world stays in the cool Pandora palette to read as the gentle, even-temperature case.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no arrows, no grid, no diagram chrome, no 3D-render or photographic look, no lens flares
